encounters.cc: Six-month history of progressive joint pain and stiffness in knees and hands, with tightening of wedding ring and increase in shoe size.

lines: Six-month history of progressive joint pain and stiffness in knees and hands, with tightening of wedding ring and increase in shoe size.
He reports that his symptoms are most pronounced in the morning and involve his knees and hands.
He also mentions that his wedding ring no longer fits, and he has noticed an increase in shoe size.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
On examination, his blood pressure is 140/85 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm
He appears to have an enlarged jaw and tongue.
His hands are noted to have soft tissue swelling, and his knee examination reveals bony enlargement with preserved range of motion.
- Oral glucose tolerance test: No suppression of GH
Radiographs of the hands and knees show widened joint spaces without significant osteophyte formation.

encounters.cc: Two-month history of persistent sinusitis unresponsive to antibiotics, productive cough with occasional hemoptysis, and 10-pound unintentional weight loss.

lines: Two-month history of persistent sinusitis unresponsive to antibiotics, productive cough with occasional hemoptysis, and 10-pound unintentional weight loss.

This 50-year-old male with a history of acromegaly diagnosed six months prior presents to the Pulmonology clinic with a 2-month history of persistent sinusitis unresponsive to antibiotics, a productive cough with occasional hemoptysis, and a 10-pound unintentional weight loss.
He also reports generalized malaise and a new onset of joint pains.
He takes albuterol inhaler as needed.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
Diffuse wheezes on lung auscultation. There is no skin rash noted.
Urinalysis shows red blood cell casts, and serum creatinine is elevated at 2.8 mg/dL from a baseline of 1.0 mg/dL a year ago.
His complete blood count reveals normocytic anemia, and his erythrocyte sedimentation rate is elevated.
Chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral nodular infiltrates.

encounters.cc: Two-week history of fatigue, decreased urine output, and new-onset bilateral lower extremity edema with dark-colored urine.

lines: Two-week history of fatigue, decreased urine output, and new-onset bilateral lower extremity edema with dark-colored urine.

The patient is a 51-year-old male with a history of granulomatosis with polyangiitis who presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fatigue, decreased urine output, and new-onset swelling in his lower extremities.
He also reports dark-colored urine over the past 3 days.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
He denies sinus congestion, ear pain, or rashes.
Vital signs show blood pressure of 155/95 mm Hg.
Physical exam reveals bilateral crackles in the lungs and 2+ pitting edema in both legs.
Urinalysis shows proteinuria and numerous red blood cells.
Serum creatinine is 4.6 mg/dL, and C-reactive protein is elevated.

encounters.cc: Severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back with nausea and vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption.

lines: Severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back with nausea and vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption.

The patient with acromegaly, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, microscopic polyangiitis, and alcohol use disorder presents to the emergency department with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back that started 24 hours ago, associated with nausea and vomiting.
He admits to heavy alcohol consumption over the past week.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
On examination, his temperature is 38.3°C (100.9°F), heart rate is 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg.
His abdomen is distended, with diffuse tenderness and decreased bowel sounds.
Abdominal ultrasound shows no gallstones or biliary ductal dilatation.
The patient's condition deteriorates over the next 48 hours with persistent hypotension despite aggressive fluid resuscitation, oliguria, and increasing oxygen requirements.

encounters.cc: Abrupt-onset severe headache described as 'worst headache of life' with associated nausea, blurred vision, and confusion.

lines: Abrupt-onset severe headache described as 'worst headache of life' with associated nausea, blurred vision, and confusion.
The patient with known pituitary macroadenoma and systemic vasculitides presents with acute neurological symptoms.
He describes it as the "worst headache" he has ever experienced, with associated nausea and blurred vision.
His wife reports that he seemed confused and had difficulty recognizing objects around him.
He has a history of hypertension and was recently evaluated for progressive fatigue, decreased libido, and mild weight gain, but no treatment was initiated.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
Temperature is 36.8 °C (98.2 °F), blood pressure is 88/54 mmHg, pulse is 118/min, and respiratory rate is 22/min.
On examination, the patient is diaphoretic and restless.
He has bilateral ptosis with impaired extraocular movements and reduced peripheral vision.
The heart and lungs are clear.
Laboratory studies show mild hyponatremia and hypoglycemia.
MRI of the brain reveals an enlarged sellar mass with evidence of recent hemorrhage.

encounters.cc: Nausea, vomiting, and lethargy diagnosed one week after high-grade B-cell lymphoma diagnosis and two days prior to scheduled chemotherapy.

lines: Nausea, vomiting, and lethargy diagnosed one week after high-grade B-cell lymphoma diagnosis and two days prior to scheduled chemotherapy.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of acromegaly secondary to pituitary macroadenoma, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, microscopic polyangiitis, alcohol use disorder, and recent pituitary apoplexy who presents with nausea, vomiting, and lethargy.
He was diagnosed with high-grade B-cell lymphoma one week ago and is scheduled to start chemotherapy in two days.
He reports no fever, cough, or diarrhea.
- Pituitary apoplexy with secondary adrenal insufficiency (adrenal crisis) (diagnosed 2022-05-15)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
Blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 98 bpm
He is alert but appears fatigued.
He has no palpable lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.
- Creatinine: 2.1 mg/dL (increased from a baseline of 1.0 mg/dL)
An electrocardiogram shows peaked T waves.

encounters.cc: Nausea, vomiting, lethargy, and muscle cramps occurring 48 hours after receiving first cycle of R-CHOP chemotherapy.

lines: Nausea, vomiting, lethargy, and muscle cramps occurring 48 hours after receiving first cycle of R-CHOP chemotherapy.
The 52-year-old with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and prior tumor lysis syndrome presents 48 hours after his first R-CHOP cycle.
He appears fatigued and complains of muscle cramps.
- Pituitary apoplexy with secondary adrenal insufficiency (adrenal crisis) (diagnosed 2022-05-15)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, pulse is 98/min, and respirations are 18/min.
Physical examination reveals mild flank tenderness.
An electrocardiogram shows peaked T waves.

encounters.cc: Severe pain and limited range of motion in right shoulder after falling from a ladder onto the shoulder.

lines: Severe pain and limited range of motion in right shoulder after falling from a ladder onto the shoulder.
The patient with acromegaly, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma presents after a fall.
He reports that he landed directly on his shoulder and felt immediate pain.
After reduction of the dislocation, the patient still has difficulty with shoulder abduction and weakness on resisted external rotation.
- Pituitary apoplexy with secondary adrenal insufficiency (adrenal crisis) (diagnosed 2022-05-15)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN for shortness of breath
Alcohol: Chronic heavy daily use, 6-12 beers per day with recent binge episodes.
The right shoulder appears squared off and there is a prominent acromion.
There is tenderness over the anterior aspect of the shoulder.
The patient is unable to abduct his right arm beyond 30 degrees and has weakness on resisted external rotation.
There is no sensory deficit noted in the affected arm.
An X-ray of the shoulder shows an anterior dislocation without fracture.
